summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identity on install
details: The @myorder-frontend-commons/analytics package claims a previously-unclaimed npm scope with a stub index.js whose exported function names mirror an internal library, so a misconfigured build resolving this public package in place of the private one does not fail. On install, a postinstall script (poc.js) collects os.hostname(), os.userInfo(), os.platform()/arch/release, cwd, node version, package version, and the names of CI-related environment variables, and transmits them to an attacker-controlled interactsh (OAST) subdomain db4jftohu4noreqdanngpnb3ger45ykrt.oast.fun via an HTTP GET to /beacon/<token>. The hostname and username are additionally hex-encoded into the DNS label, so a bare DNS lookup leaks installer identity even when outbound HTTP is blocked. Any build or CI environment that resolves this package discloses host and user identification to a third-party collector at install time.
